name: Coconut Chutney

ingredients.name: hot water, divided, plus more as needed
Resham Patti powder, plus more to taste

instructions.primary_message: In a small heatproof bowl, combine tamarind pulp and 1/4 cup hot water. Using a fork, break tamarind into small pieces. Let soak until softened, about 15 minutes. Using a fork, squeeze and mash tamarind into water until combined. Set a fine-mesh strainer over a medium bowl. Strain tamarind mixture over prepared strainer, pressing on the solids with a rubber spatula to extract as much tamarind paste as possible; discard any fibrous bits or seeds.

In a blender, combine tamarind paste, coconut, garlic, chile powder, cumin, sugar, salt, and remaining 1/4 cup water. Blend until smooth and thick, about 2 minutes, stopping to scrape down sides of blender as needed. If the mixture is too thick to blend, add more water, 1 tablespoon at a time, as needed, until the chutney forms a thick, smooth, spoonable paste.
Season with additional salt and chile powder to taste. Transfer chutney to an airtight container or serve immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: coconut garlic chutney, coconut chutney, tamarind chutney, Indian coconut chutney, tamarind coconut chutney

description: This creamy coconut chutney is made with tamarind, chile, cumin, and fresh coconut for a tangy, spicy, boldly garlicky condiment.
notes:
Optional substitutions: Resham Patti powder → Indian red chile powder

Notes: If using frozen shredded coconut, thaw according to package instructions before using.
Resham Patti and other Indian red chile powders can be found at Indian grocery stores or online. If unavailable, substitute cayenne pepper, starting with 1/4 teaspoon and adding more to taste. Do not use American chili powder blend, which usually contains cumin, garlic powder, oregano, and other seasonings.

Make-ahead and storage: The chutney can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Kaumudi Marathé
